notes: The second whom is given to the resumptive suffix of the coordinated clause rather than to the one written relative, per rule 22's coordinated-clause paragraph; the competing reading distributes the relative under rule 55.

The first clause's object suffix is unrepresented under rule 22's opening sentence: the ASV writes one Whom, and rule 22's fusion exception reaches pronominal adverbs and whose, not an object suffix beside a bare relative.
אִישׁ חֲסִידֶךָ is split, not fused: the ASV spends a word on each morpheme (one, godly), so rule 30's one-English-word condition is unmet and rule 2 governs.
